lead: GSM is the second-generation cellular system that carries voice as a circuit. GPRS keeps the same towers and core but adds packet data for Internet use. UMTS keeps the core and changes the radio to wideband CDMA. Phones still fall back to these networks for voice, SMS, and older data services. For an app developer, coverage, data speed, and circuit versus packet behaviour decide what an app can do. The parts below are the ones exams ask for.
prereq: You need: Chapter 1.2 for where 2G and 3G sit in the timeline.

sections.h3: GSM: mobile station, base station subsystem, network subsystem

blocks.text: GSM divides the network into three parts. The mobile station (MS) is the handset plus the SIM. The ME is the handset hardware; the SIM holds the subscriber identity (IMSI) and the authentication key. The base station subsystem (BSS) is the radio access network. It has the BTS (base transceiver station), the tower and radio unit, and the BSC (base station controller), which assigns radio channels and manages handover between BTSs. The network subsystem (NSS) switches calls and stores subscriber data. The MSC (mobile switching centre) connects calls to the PSTN. The VLR (visitor location register) is a temporary copy of subscriber data for the area an MSC serves. The HLR (home location register) is the permanent home record: subscription, services, and the current VLR address. The AUC (authentication centre) supplies keys for checking the SIM. The EIR (equipment identity register) lists stolen or blocked handset identities. Interfaces have names: Um between MS and BTS, Abis between BTS and BSC, A between BSC and MSC. The split lets radio vendors and switch vendors work separately, and it keeps billing and roaming data in a few central databases. On the radio side, GSM uses 200 kHz carriers. Each carrier is shared by frequency division (FDMA) and by time division (TDMA).

blocks.where: T<sub>slot</sub> is one time slot in ms; T<sub>frame</sub> = 4.615 ms is the frame length; f<sub>frame</sub> is the frame rate in frames per second. With 8 slots per frame, T<sub>slot</sub> = 576.875 µs and f<sub>frame</sub> = 216.7 frames per second. A voice call reserves one slot for the whole call, even during silence.

sections.h3: GPRS: packets added to the GSM core

blocks.text: GPRS adds packet switching to the GSM network without replacing the towers or the MSC. Two new nodes matter. The SGSN (serving GPRS support node) serves the mobile in its routing area. It authenticates the user, tracks the mobile, and forwards packets to the right BSS. The GGSN (gateway GPRS support node) is the gateway to external packet networks such as the Internet. It assigns the mobile an IP address and hides the mobile's location from the outside network. A PDP context is the session record that maps the mobile's IP address to a tunnel between SGSN and GGSN. To use data, the phone first attaches to the SGSN, then activates a PDP context. After that the connection is always-on: there is no dial-up step for each app, and packets are sent only when there is data. The same GSM time slots carry both voice and GPRS packets, so the operator divides capacity between them. Circuit switching holds a slot for the whole call; packet switching shares slots and sends only when needed.

UMTS is the 3G system that keeps the GSM/GPRS core and changes the radio access. The new radio network is UTRAN (UMTS terrestrial radio access network). It has Node B, the 3G base station, and the RNC (radio network controller), which controls several Node Bs and manages radio resources. The air interface is WCDMA (wideband code division multiple access). WCDMA uses 5 MHz carriers. All users share the same carrier at the same time, and each user is separated by a code. The wide band gives a high chip rate, which spreads each signal and makes the receiver resistant to narrowband interference. UMTS introduces soft handover. In soft handover, the phone is connected to two or more Node Bs at the same time, and the RNC combines the received signals. The call is not dropped at the cell edge because the new link is made before the old one is broken. Handover signalling details are in Chapter 1.5. UMTS data rates are higher than GPRS, and later HSPA upgrades raise them further. The core still uses MSC and VLR for voice and SGSN and GGSN for packets.

spec.aria: A grid of 4 rows (carriers) by 8 columns (time slots); one cell is marked control and the other 31 are calls; braces show one slot of 576.875 microseconds and one frame of 4.615 milliseconds.

examples.question: A GSM cell has 4 carriers. Each carrier has 8 time slots in a 4.615 ms frame. One slot in the whole cell is reserved for the control channel. (a) How many calls can run at once? (b) What is the frame rate? (c) How long is one time slot?
steps: Total time slots = 4 carriers × 8 slots per carrier = 32 slots.
Traffic slots = 32 − 1 control slot = 31. So 31 calls can run at once.
Frame rate = 1 ÷ 4.615 ms = 216.6847 frames per second ≈ 216.7 frames per second.
examples.answer: 31 calls, a frame rate of 216.7 frames per second, and a slot length of 576.875 µs.
examples.check:
carriers = 4
slots_per_carrier = 8
frame_ms = 4.615
total_slots = carriers * slots_per_carrier
calls = total_slots - 1
frame_rate = 1000 / frame_ms
slot_us = frame_ms * 1000 / slots_per_carrier
print(calls)
print(round(frame_rate, 1))
print(round(slot_us, 3))

traps: HLR and VLR: the HLR is the permanent home record; the VLR is the temporary copy for the visited area.
SGSN and GGSN: the SGSN serves the mobile; the GGSN is the gateway to the Internet.
MSC and BSC: the MSC switches calls; the BSC controls radio channels and BTS handover.
GSM uses FDMA plus TDMA on 200 kHz carriers; UMTS uses WCDMA on 5 MHz carriers.
Circuit and packet: a GSM voice call reserves a time slot; GPRS shares slots and sends only when there is data.

quiz.q: What does the SIM hold in a GSM mobile station?
quiz.a: The SIM holds the subscriber identity (IMSI) and the authentication key.

quiz.q: Why is GSM split into a base station subsystem and a network subsystem?
quiz.a: The BSS handles radio access, while the NSS switches calls and stores subscriber data. The split separates radio vendors from switch vendors and centralises billing and roaming records.

quiz.q: A GSM cell has 3 carriers, each with 8 time slots in a frame. One slot in the whole cell is used for control. How many calls can run at once?
quiz.a: Total slots = 3 × 8 = 24. Traffic slots = 24 − 1 = 23. So 23 calls can run at once.

quiz.q: A GSM frame lasts 4.615 ms and has 8 time slots. How long is one time slot in microseconds?
What does the GGSN do in GPRS?
quiz.a: The GGSN is the gateway to external packet networks. It assigns the mobile an IP address and tunnels packets between the mobile network and the Internet.

quiz.q: Why is GPRS called an always-on service?
quiz.a: The phone attaches to the SGSN and activates a PDP context once. After that it keeps an IP session and sends packets only when there is data, with no dial-up step for each app.

quiz.q: How does soft handover in UMTS differ from a hard handover?
quiz.a: In soft handover the phone is connected to two or more Node Bs at the same time, and the RNC combines the signals. A hard handover breaks the old link before making the new one.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real networks still use GSM as a voice and SMS fallback, while GPRS and UMTS carry older machine and handset traffic. UMTS later gained HSPA, which raised packet speeds without changing the 5 MHz WCDMA radio. The same core ideas appear in 4G as the HSS, MME and packet gateway. Search next for GSM MAP, the GPRS tunnelling protocol, and WCDMA spreading factor.
